problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x+y)+3{z}^{2}x$, in what direction does the function increase most rapidly at the point $(1,0,1)?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Direction of Maximum Increase or Maximum Decrease of a Function
examples.problem: In what direction does the function $f (x, y) = \ln (x^2y)$ decrease most rapidly at the point $(2, 1)?$
examples.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ decreases most rapidly in the direction opposite to that of its gradient.

So, we compute $-\nabla f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(2,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-∇f(x,y) & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}y))\text{ }i-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}y))\text{ }j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}y}\cdot 2xy\text{ }i-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}y}\cdot {x}^{2}j \\  & =-\frac{2}{x}\text{ }i-\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j \\ -∇f(2,1) & =-\frac{2}{2}\text{ }i-\frac{1}{1}\text{ }j \\  & =-i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function decreases most rapidly in the direction of $- \, \mathbf i - \mathbf j.$

feedback.problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-xy$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=i-j.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The directional derivative ${f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)$ of a function $f(x,y)$ at the point $(a,b)$ in the direction of the vector $v$ is given by

$$
{f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)=∇f(a,b)\cdot u
$$

where $u$ is a unit vector in the direction of $v.$

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{2} \\ u & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the gradient $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-xy)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-xy)j \\  & =(2x-y)\,i+(2y-x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,1) & =(2(1)-1)\,i+(2(1)-1)\,j \\  & =i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the directional derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =∇\,f(1,1)\cdot u \\  & =(i+j)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j) \\  & =\frac{1(1)+1(-1)}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
